title: The Global Findex Database 2021: Financial Inclusion, Digital Payments, and Resilience in the Age of COVID-19
authors: Asli Demirguc-Kunt, Leora Klapper, Dorothe Singer, Saniya Ansar
description: World Bank's comprehensive database finding that 76% of adults globally had a bank or mobile money account in 2021, up from 51% in 2011, with mobile money driving inclusion gains in Sub-Saharan Africa, though gender and income gaps persist.

title: The Miracle of Microfinance? Evidence from a Randomized Evaluation
authors: Abhijit Banerjee, Esther Duflo, Rachel Glennerster, Cynthia Kinnan
description: RCT in Hyderabad, India finding that access to microcredit led to modest increases in business investment and profits among existing entrepreneurs but did not lead to transformative effects on average household income, health, or women's empowerment.

title: State of the Industry Report on Mobile Money 2023
description: GSMA annual report on the mobile money industry, documenting that the number of registered mobile money accounts surpassed 1.6 billion globally, with transaction values exceeding $1.26 trillion, and that mobile money continues to drive financial inclusion in underserved markets.

title: Financial Inclusion: Overview
description: World Bank overview of financial inclusion as a development priority, summarizing the evidence that access to financial services enables poor households to manage risk, invest in opportunities, and build resilience to economic shocks.

title: Microfinance and Poverty: Evidence Using Panel Data from Bangladesh
description: Panel data study finding that microfinance in Bangladesh helped reduce poverty among participants and generated positive spillovers to non-participants in program villages, with larger effects for extreme poverty and for female borrowers.

title: Expanding Access to Finance: Good Practices and Policies for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises
description: Comprehensive review of policies and practices for expanding financial access for MSMEs in developing countries, analyzing the roles of credit registries, secured transactions, bank competition, and innovative lending technologies in closing the MSME finance gap.

title: Financial Inclusion and Development: A Cross Country Analysis
description: Foundational cross-country analysis using the first Global Findex data to document financial inclusion patterns across 148 countries, identifying income, education, gender, and age as key determinants of financial access and revealing large within-country inequalities.

title: Financial Education Programs and Interventions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
description: Meta-analysis of 76 RCTs on financial education, finding that financial education programs have small but significant effects on financial knowledge and downstream financial behaviors, with effects that are larger in lower-income countries.

title: Achieving Universal Financial Access by 2020
description: World Bank overview of its Universal Financial Access 2020 initiative, tracking progress toward the goal of enabling adults worldwide to access a transaction account, and identifying the remaining barriers including documentation, distance, and cost.

title: FinTech and Financial Inclusion in the New Normal
description: Examines how FinTech innovations accelerated by COVID-19 are reshaping financial inclusion, analyzing the roles of digital lending, insurtech, blockchain-based remittances, and regulatory sandboxes in expanding access while managing emerging risks.

title: Remittances and Financial Inclusion: Evidence from El Salvador
description: Examines the relationship between remittances and financial inclusion in El Salvador, finding that remittance recipients are more likely to have bank accounts and that digital remittance channels can serve as an entry point for broader financial service use.

title: The Little Data Book on Financial Inclusion 2022
description: Pocket edition of Global Findex indicators for over 140 economies, providing country-level data on account ownership, digital payment use, savings and borrowing behavior, and the remaining barriers to financial inclusion across regions and demographics.

title: National Financial Inclusion Strategies: Current State of Practice
description: Reviews the experience of over 60 countries that have adopted national financial inclusion strategies, analyzing common elements including targets, coordination mechanisms, and regulatory reforms, and identifying lessons for effective strategy implementation.

title: The Global Findex Database 2021
description: The definitive demand-side data on how adults save, borrow, make payments, and manage risk—covering 123 economies.

title: Financial Inclusion and Digital Financial Services
description: CGAP's research portfolio on branchless banking, agent networks, and consumer protection in inclusive finance.

title: The State of Economic Inclusion Report 2021
description: The first global stocktaking of 'graduation' and economic-inclusion programs reaching over 90 million people.

title: Banking the World: Empirical Foundations of Financial Inclusion
authors: Robert Cull, Asli Demirguc-Kunt, Jonathan Morduch
description: A landmark edited volume assembling the empirical evidence on access to finance for the poor.

title: Portfolios of the Poor: How the World's Poor Live on $2 a Day
authors: Daryl Collins, Jonathan Morduch, Stuart Rutherford, Orlanda Ruthven
description: The 'financial diaries' study revealing the sophisticated money management of poor households across India, Bangladesh, and South Africa.

title: Six Randomized Evaluations of Microcredit
authors: Abhijit Banerjee, Dean Karlan, Jonathan Zinman
description: The synthesis showing that microcredit expands business activity but has modest average effects on income and well-being.

title: Digital Financial Services and Inclusion
description: Reviews how mobile money and fintech are reshaping access to finance in developing economies.

title: Advancing Women's Financial Inclusion
description: The Mobile Gender Gap Report analysing the barriers women face in accessing mobile and digital financial services.

title: Is Mobile Money Changing Rural Africa? Evidence from a Field Experiment
description: A randomised introduction of mobile money in rural Mozambican villages. Remittances received and household welfare rise, especially under floods and idiosyncratic shocks, and migration out of the villages rises with agricultural activity and investment falling. Read it for the second half, which most citations omit.

title: Mobile Money, Financial Inclusion, and Unmet Opportunities: Evidence from Uganda
authors: Jana S. Hamdan, Katharina Lehmann-Uschner, Lukas Menkhoff
description: 86 per cent of the microentrepreneurs sampled own a mobile money account and 49 per cent use it. The gap is the finding. A choice experiment attributes much of it to fees, agent density and low price sensitivity from thin financial education.

title: Fintech and Savings in African Countries: The Case of Mobile Money
description: Harmonised FinScope surveys from Malawi, Tanzania and Uganda across 2013, 2017 and 2021, instrumented on distance to the nearest agent. The contribution is the decomposition: mobile money moves saving onto digital platforms and away from banks and ROSCAs rather than simply raising the amount saved.

title: Do financial innovations improve financial inclusion? Evidence from mobile money adoption in Africa
authors: Désiré Avom, Chrysost Bangaké, Hermann Ndoya
description: Panel of 50 African countries, 2004 to 2020, with propensity score matching putting the effect of mobile money adoption on financial inclusion at 12 to 14 per cent. Macro counterpart to the household-level trials.

title: From expanding financial services to tackling poverty in West African Economic and Monetary Union: The accelerating role of mobile money
authors: Melain Modeste Senou, Denis Acclassato Houensou
description: Uses Findex data and a recursive bivariate probit across the WAEMU countries. Separates the purpose of use (saving, borrowing, remittance) rather than treating mobile money as one thing.

title: Mobile money, and the welfare of women and youths in fragile states: Evidence from Mozambique
description: 900 households from the 2019 FinScope survey in a post-conflict, climate-exposed setting. Welfare gains run through active usage, not account ownership. The authors state plainly that their instrument cannot be fully tested, which is worth more than the point estimate.

title: Assessing household confidence in saving with banks and MNO-led mobile money: evidence from the household survey in Tanzania
authors: Goodluck Charles, Renger Kanani, Neema Mori
description: 9,915 FinScope respondents. Households trust banks with savings more than mobile network operators, and education and location both shift that. A corrective to the assumption that an account is an account.
